title: Do Not Say Goodnight
summary: A late-night radio host has one rule for her listeners: never say goodnight out loud. Tonight a caller breaks it.

beats.text: This is Port Ellis Night Radio. Tonight's rule: never say goodnight out loud. Not once.
Goodnight is what the sirens whisper before the infected come running.
A caller is on line one. She says her son is asleep upstairs and will not wake.
lines: He hasn't moved since last night.

beats.text: She wants to kiss him goodnight. Just once. I beg her not to.
lines: I just want to say it to him.

beats.text: Through the speakers, faintly, a woman's voice: "Goodnight, sweetheart."
Every figure on my street turned toward the sound. Then, slowly, they began to kneel.
One by one they lay down on the wet road and closed their eyes. They were sleeping.
The siren was never the signal. Goodnight was the cure.
On line one, a small voice whispered, "Mum? Is the city asleep now?" I whispered back: "Goodnight."
